# markup.nvim engine

The native half of markup.nvim, in Rust: the node tree, layout, paint and
the diff that becomes buffer patches. For working on the engine; plugins
use it through the Lua API in [api/](api/README.md).

## `lib.rs`

*lua/markup/core/lib.rs*

Native core of markup.nvim.

Lua owns reactivity and everything that talks to Neovim. This crate owns the
retained node tree and turns it into line patches:

```text
commands -> tree -> layout -> paint -> diff -> patches
```

Only `engine::protocol` and `engine::lua` know about Lua. No Lua handle is
stored between calls, so the tree is plain data and mlua's limit of roughly
8000 live handles under LuaJIT cannot be reached.

## `engine/cursor.rs`

*lua/markup/core/engine/cursor.rs*

Moves a cursor between interactive nodes, for menus and lists of buttons.

```rust
pub fn snap(&self, from: (i32, i32), to: (i32, i32), text: bool) -> Option<(i32, i32)>
```

Where a cursor that moved from `from` to `to` should land. Stays inside
an interactive node, otherwise jumps to the nearest one in the direction
of travel, and goes back when there is none. One press always reaches the
next node, in any direction, since moving inside one shows nothing.
Positions are `(row, col)`.

With `text`, text counts as well. The column then survives the jump, and
with nothing ahead the nearest text wins, so that `gg` still gets there.
0

## `engine/diff.rs`

*lua/markup/core/engine/diff.rs*

Works out the smallest set of line replacements between two frames.

```rust
pub struct Patch<'a>
```

Replaces lines `first..last` of the previous frame with `lines`.
0

```rust
pub fn diff<'a>(old: &[Line], new: &'a [Line]) -> Vec<Patch<'a>>
```

Trims the unchanged start and end. When the middle kept its length it is
split into runs of changed lines, otherwise it becomes one replacement.
Patches are in order and their ranges refer to the previous frame, so
applying them from last to first keeps every range valid.
0

## `engine/layout/wrap.rs`

*lua/markup/core/engine/layout/wrap.rs*

Line breaking for a run of inline content.

The whole run wraps as one piece of text: a line can break inside any span,
and a word split across two spans stays together. Each text node then holds
the fragments it was cut into, and each inline element the area it covers
on every line, which is what paint draws highlights over.

```rust
pub enum RunItem
```

What a run of inline content holds: nodes, and the edges of an inline that
is split around the blocks inside it, as CSS splits one.
0

```rust
pub fn flow(tree: &mut Tree, run: &[Index], limit: i32, available: i32, split_words: bool) -> Size
```

Flows a run of nodes, breaking lines past `limit`; see `flow_items`.
0

```rust
pub fn flow_items( tree: &mut Tree, items: &[RunItem], limit: i32, available: i32, split_words: bool, ) -> Size
```

Lays out a run of inline nodes in `limit` cells at the origin of the run.
Flows a run of inline nodes, breaking lines past `limit`. Whatever cannot
flow, such as a block among them, is laid out for `available`, which a run
that never breaks still needs: `limit` is then unbounded, and a child as
wide as its parent would be that wide too. Without `split_words`, a word
longer than a line runs past it whole.
0

## `engine/protocol.rs`

*lua/markup/core/engine/protocol.rs*

Wire format between Lua and the engine.

Lua appends commands to one flat array and sends it once per frame, so a
frame costs a single boundary crossing however much changed:

```text
{ opcode, arg, arg, opcode, arg, ... }
```

The opcodes mirror `lua/markup/view/protocol.lua`. Patches return as tables
of strings and flat integer arrays, with highlights as interned ids.

```rust
pub fn decode( ops: &LuaTable, len: usize, mut apply: impl FnMut(Command) -> LuaResult<()>, ) -> LuaResult<()>
```

Decodes the first `len` values of `ops` and passes each command to `apply`.
0

```rust
pub fn encode_node(lua: &Lua, info: &NodeInfo) -> LuaResult<LuaTable>
```

Builds the table devtools read for one node.
0

```rust
pub fn encode( lua: &Lua, patches: &[Patch], timings: Timings, errors: &[String], ) -> LuaResult<LuaTable>
```

Builds the frame table returned to Lua.

```lua
{
  patches = { { first, last, lines = { ... }, marks = { row, start, end, hl, ... } } },
  layout = 0.1, paint = 0.2, diff = 0.3,
}
```
Errors are the commands that could not be applied, such as one for a node
that is gone, each said once.
0

*lua/markup/core/engine/tree.rs*

Retained node tree, stored in a slab.

Clients name nodes with ids of their own choosing, so creating a node needs
no answer from the engine. Inside the tree nodes link by slab index, which
is what layout and paint use.
